scenario.scenario_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
scenario.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, which means a UAV is already inside your medium ring the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything flying under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. There is a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. Your magazine is finite and the assessment counts rounds expended.

IFF interrogation is unavailable on this fit — there is no transponder reply on any track. Identification comes from system classification and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy.

The raid is already on top of you as you take the seat. Fast closers are at the edge of the long ring in the first seconds and mixed-class tracks appear continuously through the first minute, with arrivals that overlap rather than queue. You have 230 seconds and there are not enough rounds to be careless. Sequence the queue, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in flight (hard system limit)
Commander referral response time for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer, held from the first sweep and only 4 km outside the long ring. First valid solution of the run at about T+14; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+187 if unengaged.
Second fast closer, also up at zero. Reaches the long-range ring at about T+22 — while the first engagement is almost certainly still in flight.
High and fastest of the three; enters the long-range ring at about T+35, when the two-in-flight limit is most likely saturated by the first two.

First of the unmanned wave, appearing inside the short ring while the lead jet is still short of the long ring. Reads as the nearest and most urgent track on the display; reaches the 5 km inner limit at about T+85.
Steady inbound profile, no manoeuvre. Inner limit at about T+107, with the jet queue still running.
Low-mid altitude; marginal against a badly set tilt. Inner limit at about T+129.
Arrives with the tail of the jet wave still being serviced. Inner limit at about T+144.
Southern flank, low, just inside the short ring on appearance. Inner limit at about T+168.
Fastest of the unmanned wave, northern edge of the sector. Inner limit at about T+176, in the middle of the mop-up.
Last hostile to appear, near the southern sector edge and low — easy to leave unserviced. Inner limit at about T+217, right at the end of the run.

Never resolves unaided. Appears inside the medium ring with a valid solution available immediately, closing hard with heading and altitude changes that read as an attack run; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+66 and the inner limit near T+128. Classification must be referred to the commander; behaviour is not a classification.
Low and slow on the southern flank; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. Correlates to an own-force call sign at about T+55.
Appears inside the short ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave, just as the UAV queue builds. Resolves only at about T+95, after more than a minute of ambiguity.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers and destroyed inside the 230-second window; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles reaching the 5 km inner limit unserviced; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown or a friendly is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. No more than eleven interceptors may be expended.

result.notes: Compressed as far as the profile physically allows: the run floor is set by the 600 kt jet in the raid crossing the 70 km long-range ring (227 s), so ninety seconds is unreachable without deleting the fast closers that the dilemma is built on — I cut the window from 315 s to 230 s instead and made every arrival earlier and closer. All three jets now spawn 74–79 km (just outside the long ring) so first valid solutions fall at T+14/T+22/T+35 instead of T+16/T+29/T+47; the UAV wave spawns 14–22 km rather than 13–31 km with appearances at T+12 through T+60 (was T+15–92), putting the seven hostile inner-limit deadlines at roughly T+85, 107, 129, 144, 168, 176 and 217 instead of a T+157–193 pile-up; and the two resolving Unknowns come back at T+55 and T+95 instead of T+110 and T+150. Nothing else — composition, bearings, the referral rule, the scoring hierarchy — was touched.
requests: The window is far too long and nothing happens for the first two minutes. Bring the arrivals forward.
Far too long. Make the whole exercise about ninety seconds.
adjustments: The run is 315 seconds rather than the 230 asked for. Any shorter and the fastest track would start already inside the engagement envelope, leaving nothing to identify on the way in.
